{"id": "28:22/q19", "question": "What did Moses know about the roads, and which did he take?", "turns_on": "The reports differ about whether he had entered a road, how many roads appeared, and how he selected the route.", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q19/p1", "position": "He did not know the road; he trusted God to bring him to the right one.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās repeatedly says he relied on good expectation of God. Muqātil says he feared losing the route without a guide; Ibn Isḥāq says God prepared it. Abū Ḥayyān prefers the apparent sense of direct divine guidance to safety. Ibn ʿĀshūr says he reached a Midian road after wandering."}, {"id": "28:22/q19/p2", "position": "Four roads appeared, and he chose the Midian road after praying.", "reasons": "ʿIkrima says he could not tell which of the four to take; Mawardī specifies he prayed when they diverged."}, {"id": "28:22/q19/p3", "position": "Three roads appeared; he chose the middle, while pursuers took the two sides.", "reasons": "Bayḍāwī says he chose it in trust and good expectation; Bursevī says pursuers reasoned a fugitive would avoid the central route. Biqāʿī says they expected him on side roads or cross-country paths."}, {"id": "28:22/q19/p4", "position": "He had already entered the Midian road and prayed to stay straight on it.", "reasons": "Mawardī reports this from Qatāda and al-Suddī; Ibn Kathīr calls the road well traveled."}, {"id": "28:22/q19/p5", "position": "He deliberately chose a safe road that happened to lead to Midian.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān reports this as another account."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q20", "question": "Did a being guide Moses to Midian, and who was it?", "turns_on": "Reports differ between an unnamed angel, Gabriel, and divine direction without an identified intermediary.", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q20/p1", "position": "An angel guided him.", "reasons": "Al-Suddī says the angel found him lost, mounted on a horse and sometimes carrying a spear; Moses bowed or prostrated in fear or joy, then followed. Thaʿlabī and Zamakhsharī report a mounted angel with spear; Baghawī gives a staff. Other sources simply say God sent an angel. Qurṭubī's Abū Mālik adds that Pharaoh's searchers watched the passes."}, {"id": "28:22/q20/p2", "position": "Gabriel specifically guided him.", "reasons": "Rāzī reports this from some; Qurṭubī attributes it to Muqātil and al-Suddī but leaves the truth to God. Ālūsī and Abū Ḥayyān also relay the identification."}, {"id": "28:22/q20/p3", "position": "God prepared and showed the route without a named guide.", "reasons": "Ibn Isḥāq says God prepared the road; Biqāʿī says God directed him along the main road and foiled pursuers; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī sees the prayer answered in his arrival."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q21", "question": "When and how did Moses receive his staff?", "turns_on": "Qurṭubī judges the Midian shepherding account more common and sounder than the angel's gift.", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q21/p1", "position": "The guiding angel gave it to him on the journey.", "reasons": "Qurṭubī gives this as a reported addition to Abū Mālik's account of the mounted angel with spear."}, {"id": "28:22/q21/p2", "position": "He took the staff in Midian for shepherding.", "reasons": "Qurṭubī prefers this account as more widespread and sounder."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q22", "question": "Whom did Moses meet in Midian?", "turns_on": "Whether the unnamed elder in the ensuing episode is identified as Shuʿayb.", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q22/p1", "position": "He met a man associated with Shuʿayb's people and later an elder whose daughter he married.", "reasons": "Al-Ḥasan calls Moses and the man from Shuʿayb's people the two best people on earth that day. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says he later married an unnamed elder's daughter; Jaʿfar's report says two young women brought Moses to their father after he watered for them."}, {"id": "28:22/q22/p2", "position": "The elder was the prophet Shuʿayb.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī cites some Imami and Sunni reports for the identification. Abū Saʿīd al-Kharrāz speaks of Moses' encounter with Shuʿayb as the beginning of blessings; Ibn ʿĀshūr says he would meet a prophet who taught prophetic conduct."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q23", "question": "What does Moses' prayer teach about reliance on God?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q23/p1", "position": "He entrusted himself to God despite fear and ignorance of the route.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās repeatedly mentions his good expectation; Ibn ʿAṭiyya sees knowledge of God and bestowed wisdom; Qushayrī describes reliance on divine opening. Iṣlāḥī says this flight, unlike his later migration as a prophet, had no divinely fixed stages, so it models guidance for truth seekers without clear promises. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says his sequence of prayers and commitments in 28:17 and 28:21 shows he sought God's approval even in natural needs."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q24", "question": "How does this flight relate to Abraham's migration?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q24/p1", "position": "Moses' prayer echoes Abraham's departure and trust in divine guidance.", "reasons": "Rāzī compares Abraham's 'I am going to my Lord; He will guide me' at 37:99 and says Moses often echoes Abraham in argument, reply, prayer and supplication. Ibn ʿĀshūr compares Abraham's migration at 29:26 and says Moses was guided to Midian, where he would meet a prophet."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q25", "question": "How does this scene connect to the surrounding story?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q25/p1", "position": "It bridges Moses' escape from Egypt to the Midian episode and God's answers to his prayers.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr reads the opening clause as coordinating with omitted wandering after he left the city. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī summarizes the flight, arrival and marriage, then says God answered three prayers: safety, the Midian road, and provision through watering, livelihood and a wife. Baghawī reports Ibn ʿAbbās calling this journey Moses' first trial."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q26", "question": "Why do tellings of Moses and Pharaoh vary across the Quran?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q26/p1", "position": "Each telling has a distinct nuance in wording, order and detail.", "reasons": "Burhān contrasts repeated Moses narratives, including Qasas 28:3–43, with Joseph's story collected in one sura; he says earlier scripture's single separate tellings differ from this Quranic pattern."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q27", "question": "What broader lesson does the Midian episode offer its audience?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q27/p1", "position": "Its virtues prepare Moses for revelation and invite emulation and recognition of prophetic character.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr lists generosity, aid to the distressed, compassion, modesty, gratitude, chastity and fidelity; Shuʿayb shows hospitality, protection and gentleness. He says Meccan polytheists could compare Moses with Muhammad's known premission virtue, while Muslims should emulate prophetic conduct."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q28", "question": "How does the verse's hope fit the rhetoric of al-Qasas?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q28/p1", "position": "Hope is characteristic of al-Qasas, compared with certainty in al-Naml.", "reasons": "Sāmarrāʾī counts ten expressions of hope in Qasas against two in Naml, citing 27:7 and 27:46."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q29", "question": "Was Moses' earlier confession a change from unbelief?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q29/p1", "position": "No; he was already a believer, and confessed the killing of the Egyptian.", "reasons": "Sāmarrāʾī contrasts the Queen of Sheba, who left sun worship and submitted to God (27:44), with Moses' admission concerning the killing (28:16, 28:21–22)."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q30", "question": "Is the sura containing this verse Meccan?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q30/p1", "position": "All of al-Qasas is Meccan.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jawzī reports this from Ḥasan, ʿAṭāʾ and ʿIkrima."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q31", "question": "What does the Quran's rhetoric require of its hearers?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q31/p1", "position": "Its inimitability is recognized directly by those fully versed in eloquent speech; others infer it according to their knowledge.", "reasons": "Bāqillānī says the first Muslims accepted from insight; foreigners infer Arab incapacity, intermediate speakers infer the limits of top experts, and skill in poetry, sermons or letters alone is insufficient. A complete rhetor hears the proof immediately; requiring the Prophet to test all Arabs would misstate it. Ibn ʿĀshūr says verse endings challenged eloquent leaders, establishing proof for them and ordinary hearers."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q32", "question": "How do interrogative forms express rejection or rebuke?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q32/p1", "position": "Their force varies with tense, word order and whether the rejected act occurred.", "reasons": "Burhān says an interrogative imperfect can deny an act or warn against it (11:28); object fronting questions the actor's fitness (6:14, 6:40); rejection may imply a false claim (37:153, 52:35, 6:100, 43:19). He distinguishes denial of an unreal act from rebuke of a real blameworthy one (37:95; 10:106; 37:86; 26:165–166; 2:188)."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q33", "question": "How should Quranic pause marks be evaluated?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q33/p1", "position": "Pauses are graded by meaning and no location has a universally obligatory or forbidden stop.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr reports Ibn al-Jazarī and classifies pauses as emphatic, good or lesser. He notes preferences for stopping at completed speech and shorter pauses before completion; he finds Ibn al-Naḥḥās's appeal to an Ibn ʿUmar report for obligatory stops unclear. Later scholars marked pauses to ease reading as Islam spread; their choices proposed interpretations. He names Ibn al-Anbārī, Ibn al-Naḥḥās, al-Nakzawī and al-Hi

{"id": "28:22/q34", "question": "How is the hāʾ in tawajjaha treated in imāla?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q34/p1", "position": "The original hāʾ itself is not inclined.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jazarī says it has no yāʾ origin, unlike an alif; a pronoun hāʾ is likewise not inclined and the preceding letter already has kasra. He contrasts ṣalāh and zakāh, whose alif cannot be inclined without the prior consonant, with tawrāh and muzjāh, whose alif derives from yāʾ. Al-Dānī assigns inclination to the alif and prior letter, with secondary coloring of hāʾ; Makkī says the hāʾ itself is never inclined."}]}
{"id": "28:22/q35", "question": "How are possessive yāʾs read in the related recitation lists?", "turns_on": "Different readers' treatment of first-person yāʾs across the cited set of passages.", "positions": [{"id": "28:22/q35/p1", "position": "Nāfiʿ opens twelve disputed yāʾs except maʿī ridʾan.", "reasons": "Ibn Mujāhid records this as a general recitation pattern in the passage."}, {"id": "28:22/q35/p2", "position": "Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr open nine, leaving three named yāʾs still.", "reasons": "Ibn Mujāhid names innī urīd, satajidunī in shāʾ Allāh, and maʿī ridʾan as exceptions."}, {"id": "28:22/q35/p3", "position": "Yaʿqūb and the Kufans keep the yāʾ still in both occurrences of laʿallī.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jazarī records this related pronoun reading."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q01", "question": "What does وَرَدَ mean here?", "turns_on": "The range of wurūd in Arabic and other Quranic passages.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q01/p1", "position": "Moses reached or approached the water, without entering it.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya compares the wider range with 19:71; al-Qurṭubī cites Zuhayr's poetry; Ibn ʿĀshūr says the arrival also marks entry into Midian's territory; al-Ālūsī excludes drinking."}, {"id": "28:23/q01/p2", "position": "Wurūd's primary sense is setting out to seek water; reaching, a water place, thirst, entering, and presence are extended uses.", "reasons": "ʿAlī b. ʿUbayd Allāh distinguishes the outward trip (wurūd) from return (ṣadr), and explains the senses of place and thirst; Ibn al-Jawzī cites 11:98, 19:71, 12:19 and 19:86 for other Quranic uses."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q02", "question": "What was مَاءَ مَدْيَنَ?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q02/p1", "position": "It was Midian's watering well or water source, where livestock were watered.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās compares it to a known local well; al-Qushayrī describes troughs; Bursawī places it three miles or less outside town; Iṣlāḥī cites the Torah's well and notes that a narrow spring would pose the same crowding problem. Ibn ʿĀshūr explains 'water' as a place name for the watering site and territory."}, {"id": "28:23/q02/p2", "position": "The water was named for Midian, son of Abraham, or for his descendant tribe.", "reasons": "Muqātil gives the eponym; al-Qurṭubī calls Midian also a tribe descended from him and cites a poem."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q03", "question": "How is مَدْيَنَ declined?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q03/p1", "position": "It is genitive in sense but diptote because it is a proper place name.", "reasons": "Al-Zajjāj, Ibn ʿAṭiyya, and al-Qurṭubī identify the town name as the reason."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q04", "question": "What does لَمَّا do in this account?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q04/p1", "position": "It marks when Moses' reaching the place was followed by finding the people there.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr states the temporal relation; al-Zarkashī describes possible responses to lammā, including a present verb with past sense, and cites 17:67, 21:12, and 11:74."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q05", "question": "What does أُمَّةً mean here?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q05/p1", "position": "A group or large crowd of people, chiefly shepherds.", "reasons": "Al-Suddī stresses its size; al-Kashshāf and al-Ālūsī describe varied people; al-Zarkashī lists other Quranic senses: leader, religion, and period (43:22; 12:45); Ibn ʿĀshūr cites 2:213."}, {"id": "28:23/q05/p2", "position": "The group numbered forty.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās supplies this count."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q06", "question": "Why does the verse say مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ?", "turns_on": "The force of the partitive phrase and its relation to the indefinite ummah.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q06/p1", "position": "It indicates the crowd comprised different kinds or classes of people.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī also reads the indefinite ummah as suggesting abundance."}, {"id": "28:23/q06/p2", "position": "It disparages the crowd as merely low people, or clarifies that they were human.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī reports both alternatives."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q07", "question": "What does وَجَدَ mean and how does its clause work?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q07/p1", "position": "It means encountered or came upon; تذودان describes the women rather than serving as another object.", "reasons": "Al-Dāmghānī and Ibn al-Jawzī compare the queen as another case of finding; al-Samīn specifies the participial clause's syntactic role."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q08", "question": "Where were the people in relation to the water?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q08/p1", "position": "At the well's rim or watering place.", "reasons": "Al-Kashshāf, al-Rāzī, Abū Ḥayyān, and al-Ālūsī interpret ʿalayhi spatially as its bank or edge."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q09", "question": "What were the crowd watering?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q09/p1", "position": "Their livestock, including sheep.", "reasons": "Ibn Isḥāq reports livestock and sheep; al-Ālūsī cautions that narrowing the animals requires a report."}, {"id": "28:23/q09/p2", "position": "The verse leaves the species of the watered beings deliberately open.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr cites al-Kashshāf and Dalāʾil al-Iʿjāz: livestock or people are possible and attention rests on the women’s withdrawal."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q10", "question": "Why did Moses come to the water?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q10/p1", "position": "He came seeking water or drink and a gathering where he could find help.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī says he intended to drink; Ibn ʿĀshūr says a newcomer naturally goes to the water to meet companions and a host."}, {"id": "28:23/q10/p2", "position": "He arrived after an exhausting eight-night walk from Egypt, hungry, barefoot, and without resources.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās says he ate leaves, lost his soles, and became so thin green matter was visible in his belly; Ibn Isḥāq adds fear, no servant, mount or provisions; Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq also reports the exhausting flight."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q11", "question": "Where were the two women relative to the crowd?", "turns_on": "Whether dūn marks lower ground or Moses' side of the crowd.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q11/p1", "position": "They were apart from the crowd, on Moses' approach side, so he encountered them first.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Qurṭubī say they were on his side; al-Biqāʿī says nearer the approach. Ibn ʿĀshūr derives dūn from 'lower' extended to a farther place and discusses min as locative with 62:9 and 3:10."}, {"id": "28:23/q11/p2", "position": "They stood below the people watering, at a lower place.", "reasons": "Al-Kashshāf and al-Rāzī take dūn spatially as lower; Abū Ḥayyān records Ibn ʿAṭiyya's competing approach-side gloss; al-Ālūsī allows below, nearby, or apart."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q12", "question": "Who were the two women?", "turns_on": "Conflicting transmitted identifications; al-Ālūsī prefers the majority identification pending reliable evidence.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q12/p1", "position": "They were daughters of the prophet Shuʿayb.", "reasons": "Muqātil calls them twins, the elder Ṣabūra and younger ʿAbrā; al-Thaʿlabī gives Shuʿayb's lineage through Buwayb and Midian. Majority attribution is reported by al-Wāḥidī and al-Ālūsī."}, {"id": "28:23/q12/p2", "position": "They were daughters of Shuʿayb's nephew.", "reasons": "Reports name the nephew Buthrūn, Yathrūn, Athrūn, Raʿāwīl or Hārūn; al-Thaʿlabī and al-Baghawī add that Shuʿayb died blind and was buried between the Maqām and Zamzam; al-Ālūsī notes conflicting reports."}, {"id": "28:23/q12/p3", "position": "They were daughters of a righteous believer of Midian, with no established kinship to Shuʿayb.", "reasons": "Al-Baghawī says he believed in Shuʿayb; al-Ālūsī treats both unrelated and nephew possibilities as unproved; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾ calls him unnamed."}, {"id": "28:23/q12/p4", "position": "The flock owner and marriage arranger was their uncle, whom they called father.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī reports this explanation from al-Baḥr."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q13", "question": "What names are given for the women?", "turns_on": "Names vary among narrative reports.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q13/p1", "position": "They were twins Ṣabūra and ʿAbrā, with Ṣabūra older by half a day.", "reasons": "Muqātil supplies the names and age detail; Ibn al-Jawzī repeats them; Abū Ḥayyān attributes them to al-Farrāʾ."}, {"id": "28:23/q13/p2", "position": "They were Layā or Liyā and Ṣafūriyā or Ṣafūrāʾ.", "reasons": "Bursawī reports al-Suhaylī’s Shafūriyya and Layya; al-Ālūsī lists ʿAbrā and Sharafā as variants of the first, Ṣafīrāʾ and Ṣafrāʾ of the second; al-Itqān says one married Moses."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q14", "question": "What does تَذُودَانِ mean in Arabic?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q14/p1", "position": "To restrain, turn back, or drive away.", "reasons": "Al-Farrāʾ restricts the ordinary object to livestock; al-Ṭabarī disputes this with a Prophetic basin report and a poet's use for people. Jarīr, Saʿīd or Suwayd b. Kurāʿ, and other verse attest restraint and repulsion; al-Naḥḥās notes leading can count as restraining. Ibn ʿĀshūr says driving stock from water is literal, people figurative, and notes uncertainty about sheep in the strict lexicon."}, {"id": "28:23/q14/p2", "position": "A dhaw

{"id": "28:23/q15", "question": "What were the women holding back, and why?", "turns_on": "The implicit object of dhāda and whether the immediate obstacle was water access, flock mixing, people, or straying.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q15/p1", "position": "They held their flock back from the water while stronger shepherds occupied it.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī prefers this because the women's answer explains delayed watering; al-Wāḥidī and al-Baghawī similarly prefer it from the context. Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Mālik, Ibn Jurayj, al-Zajjāj and others cite the men's strength; Iṣlāḥī depicts thirsty animals pressing toward water; Ibn Kathīr adds avoidance of harm."}, {"id": "28:23/q15/p2", "position": "They kept their flock separate so it would not mix with other flocks.", "reasons": "Al-Ḥasan, Yaḥyā b. Sallām and Ibn Sallām give this; al-Naḥḥās, as quoted by al-Qurṭubī, prefers it; al-Biqāʿī connects it with the women waiting."}, {"id": "28:23/q15/p3", "position": "They kept other people away from their flock.", "reasons": "Qatāda, al-Kalbī and Maʿmar's associates give this. Al-Ṭabarī argues their later answer addresses delayed watering instead; the verb can take human objects, against al-Farrāʾ's lexical restriction."}, {"id": "28:23/q15/p4", "position": "They kept their sheep from scattering or straying.", "reasons": "Al-Farrāʾ gives the livestock sense; al-Baghawī records the view but prefers that they withheld the flock from water; Abū Ṣāliḥ adds one woman held the sheep for the other."}, {"id": "28:23/q15/p5", "position": "They were shielding their faces from men looking at them.", "reasons": "Al-Kashshāf and al-Rāzī record this; al-Ālūsī calls it untenable."}, {"id": "28:23/q15/p6", "position": "They held back to avoid jostling or mixing with men.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī and al-Kashshāf report the social explanation; this can accompany holding the flock from water."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q16", "question": "Is there an expanded reading of ٱمْرَأَتَيْنِ تَذُودَانِ?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q16/p1", "position": "A reported reading supplies حابستين or حابستان, explicitly calling the women restrainers.", "reasons": "Al-Farrāʾ attributes ḥābistatān to ʿAbd Allāh; Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Qurṭubī mention codices with ḥābistatayn."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q17", "question": "Why are objects omitted from the watering and restraining verbs?", "turns_on": "Whether the unspoken object is intentionally generalized, recoverable by context, or elided for brevity.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q17/p1", "position": "The actions and agents matter; animal identity is immaterial to Moses' response.", "reasons": "ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī identifies four omissions, including Moses' later watering, and says naming sheep would wrongly narrow the lesson; his Buḥturī example shows how omission shifts focus. Al-Zamakhsharī and al-Zarkashī agree; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects reliance on Israelite material to supply sheep."}, {"id": "28:23/q17/p2", "position": "The objects remain intended and are omitted for concise expression.", "reasons": "Ibn Qutayba and al-Wāḥidī supply sheep; al-Fārisī cites 18:2 and 41:13 and poetic ellipsis; al-Sakkākī counts five omitted objects with the causative reading. Al-Jazarī argues the weak sheep heighten compassion, which al-Zarkashī disputes."}, {"id": "28:23/q17/p3", "position": "The object is left vague to prompt the listener or because context supplies it.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī offers both rhetorical explanations; al-Biqāʿī says 'we do not water' has an understood object."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q18", "question": "What did Moses ask with مَا خَطْبُكُمَا?", "turns_on": "The force of khaṭb and, in one rare reading, its vocalization.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q18/p1", "position": "He asked their situation, need, or purpose in standing apart and not watering.", "reasons": "Muqātil, Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Isḥāq connect it to their separation; the latter says he felt pity under crowd domination. Lexicographers cite a poem or Ruʾba's rajaz for khaṭb as affair; al-Māwardī and al-Jishumī say it connotes weight or importance; al-Kashshāf derives it from what one seeks, like shaʾn."}, {"id": "28:23/q18/p2", "position": "The question expressed concern and an offer to help.", "reasons": "Ibn Isḥāq describes compassion; Iṣlāḥī calls it concern rather than casual curiosity; al-Ālūsī says its gracious wording implicitly offered assistance; al-Kāshifī attributes prophetic gentleness."}, {"id": "28:23/q18/p3", "position": "With Shammar's anomalous kasra of khāʾ, he asked who their husband was and why he did not water.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān and al-Samīn call it rare; al-Ālūsī finds an objection to it unclear."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q19", "question": "How is مَا خَطْبُكُمَا parsed?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q19/p1", "position": "It is a subject and predicate question.", "reasons": "Al-Naḥḥās gives this parse; Ibn ʿĀshūr treats the speech as an explanatory substitution for the circumstance of finding the women apart."}, {"id": "28:23/q19/p2", "position": "Interrogative echo forms agree with the echoed noun in gender, number, and case.", "reasons": "Sībawayh gives ayya, ayyayn, ayya(t), and ayyāt; for a proper name he uses man ʿAbd Allāh rather than nominative ayy ʿAbd Allāh."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q20", "question": "Why did the women wait before watering?", "turns_on": "Whether practical weakness, social modesty, or both explain the delay; whether the statement is habitual.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q20/p1", "position": "They could not compete with men at the crowded water; after the shepherds departed they used leftover water in troughs.", "reasons": "Qatāda, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Isḥāq and others describe their lack of strength or inability to jostle. Muqātil says the shepherds returned to pasture first. Al-Rāzī says Moses' help let them return early; al-Ṭabarī and al-Wāḥidī mention the remaining water."}, {"id": "28:23/q20/p2", "position": "They waited out of modesty and to avoid physical mingling with men.", "reasons": "Al-Māwardī reports this independently of inability; al-Ālūsī says the wording directly signals modesty while weakness is inferred; al-Biqāʿī says their restraint shows good upbringing."}, {"id": "28:23/q20/p3", "position": "The statement describes their usual practice, not just that particular day.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī explicitly reads it habitually; Ibn ʿĀshūr says the imperfect depicts continuing abstention, though the verse does not establish a daily habit."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q21", "question": "How is لَا نَسْقِى read?", "turns_on": "Whether the verb is simple saqā or causative asqā.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q21/p1", "position": "The common reading opens nūn: nasqī from saqā.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya contrasts Ṭalḥa's reading; al-ʿĀlūsī calls it the familiar form."}, {"id": "28:23/q21/p2", "position": "A variant rounds nūn: nusqī from asqā.", "reasons": "Ṭalḥa, Ibn Masʿūd, Abū al-Jawzāʾ, Ibn Yaʿmur, Ibn Muṣarrif and others are named in the sources."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q22", "question": "How is يُصْدِرَ read and what does each reading say happens?", "turns_on": "Whether the verb is intransitive ṣadara or causative aṣdara; the readers named vary by source.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q22/p1", "position": "With ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on dāl, shepherds drive their flocks away; the object is implicit.", "reasons": "Most readers are cited for the causative; al-Naḥḥās prefers it as contextually fitter, while al-Ṭabarī accepts both. Ibn ʿĀshūr glosses it as clearing the crowd, and al-Ālūsī notes this reading does not require the men themselves to leave. Some lists of readers vary. Ibn ʿAbbās supplies the implicit result that the shepherds clear the place for the women."}, {"id": "28:23/q22/p2", "position": "With fatḥa on yāʾ and ḍamma on dāl, the shepherds themselves depart from the water.", "reasons": "Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Jaʿfar and others appear in differing source lists; al-Wāḥidī relates it to the opposite of warada and cites 99:6; al-Ālūsī notes it may emphasize avoidance of the men."}, {"id": "28:23/q22/p3", "position": "Both readings are accepted and close in overall sense.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī says recognized readers used each and both fit the scene; al-Naḥḥās nonetheless judges the causative more apt."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q23", "question": "What does ṣudūr mean as a word?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q23/p1", "position": "It means leaving or returning from the water, opposite of arriving at it.", "reasons": "Al-Māwardī links ṣadr to plans issuing forth and maṣdar to actions; al-Jishumī distinguishes causative aṣdara; al-Fārisī compares 99:6; al-Elmalılı describes moving animals away."}, {"id": "28:23/q23/p2", "position": "The causative iṣdār means making livestock or shepherds depart.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr construes clearing the crowd as the practical result."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q24", "question": "What is ٱلرِّعَآءُ grammatically?", "turns_on": "Whether riʿāʾ is analyzed as a plural formation or a collective, and whether its pattern is regular.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q24/p1", "position": "It is a plural of rāʿī, shepherd.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī lists riʿāʾ, ruʿāt, and ruʿyān; al-Zajjāj compares ṣāḥib/ṣaḥāb and others compare tājir/tujjār or qāʾim/qiyām. Al-Samīn and Abū Ḥayyān dispute al-Zamakhsharī's claim that the kasra pattern is regular for a defective participle, expecting a plural like quḍāt. Basrans and Kufans differ on deriving ruʿāt from riʿya or raʿā."}, {"id": "28:23/q24/p2", "position": "It is a collective noun, like rikhal or thanāʾ.", "reasons": "Al-Kashshāf explains its kasra by comparison with ṣiyām and qiyām; Abū Ḥayyān and al-Samīn reject the claimed regularity."}]}

{"id": "28:23/q26", "question": "What does شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ say about the father?", "turns_on": "Whether kabīr adds age alone or also status.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q26/p1", "position": "He was elderly and unable to tend, graze, draw, or water the flock, so the daughters had to do it.", "reasons": "Al-Suddī glosses advanced age; al-Kalbī says the daughters were his only helpers; al-Biqāʿī infers there were no sons able to help; al-Naḥḥās and Abū Isḥāq stress inability to go out. Al-Kashshāf defines kabīr as old."}, {"id": "28:23/q26/p2", "position": "Kabīr may describe his greatness of rank and honor as well as age.", "reasons": "Bursawī allows high rank; al-Nasafī allows state or age."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q27", "question": "Why did the women mention their father's old age?", "turns_on": "Whether the clause chiefly excuses their role, elicits assistance, or supplies a grammatical circumstance.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q27/p1", "position": "To explain and excuse their own public shepherding in place of a man.", "reasons": "Al-Māwardī, al-Wāḥidī and Ibn ʿĀshūr emphasize necessity; al-Ālūsī says he previously managed it before frailty."}, {"id": "28:23/q27/p2", "position": "To invite Moses' compassion and help without a direct request.", "reasons": "Al-Māwardī reports this alternative; al-Jishumī calls it tactful asking; Abū Ḥayyān and al-Ālūsī say their reply appealed to him indirectly."}, {"id": "28:23/q27/p3", "position": "The clause supplies a circumstance simultaneous with their waiting, or coordinates with an omitted clause.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī reports both syntactic relations."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q28", "question": "What is reported about the father's name and relation to Shuʿayb?", "turns_on": "Transmitted genealogies and names conflict; al-Ālūsī demands a reliable report before departing from the majority Shuʿayb view.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q28/p1", "position": "He is Shuʿayb himself, also called Yathrūn or Jethro in some reports.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabrisī reports this from Wahb; Ibn ʿĀshūr regards Exodus' Reuel and Jethro as names of one man and explains the Jewish priest title. Bursawī cites al-Suhaylī's identification of Yathrūn with Shuʿayb. Al-Qurṭubī notes the dispute over Shuʿayb's father's name and Qatāda's report that he was sent to al-Aykah and Midian."}, {"id": "28:23/q28/p2", "position": "He was Shuʿayb's nephew, variously called Buthrūn, Yathrūn, Athrūn, Raʿāwīl, Hārūn, or Marwān.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī lists transmitter and spelling differences, and notes a People of the Book pronunciation Yathro without final nūn."}, {"id": "28:23/q28/p3", "position": "He was Thirbī.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās gives this name without a kinship claim."}, {"id": "28:23/q28/p4", "position": "He was Yathrib or Yathrūn, master of Midian, with no specified kinship.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī records two Ibn ʿAbbās versions and says the reports conflict."}, {"id": "28:23/q28/p5", "position": "Exodus calls him Midian's priest and says he had seven daughters.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī quotes Exodus 2 and 3; Ibn ʿĀshūr reports Ibn al-ʿIbrī's seven-daughter tradition and identifies Reuel/Jethro."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q29", "question": "What happened when Moses watered for the women?", "turns_on": "Whether access required removing a stone or pressing through an open crowd, and the conflicting numbers for its weight.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q29/p1", "position": "He lifted a stone over a well that normally took ten men, then drew one bucket that sufficed.", "reasons": "ʿUmar gives the ten-men and one-bucket account; Ibn Kathīr grades its chain sound; al-Ṭabarī's and Ibn Abī Ḥātim's versions match."}, {"id": "28:23/q29/p2", "position": "He lifted a stone that a hundred men could not lift.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās says the well was covered in winter and opened in summer, and the women were astonished."}, {"id": "28:23/q29/p3", "position": "He removed a heavy stone requiring a group, variously said to be seven, ten, thirty, forty, or roughly forty men.", "reasons": "Muqātil adds a prayer for blessing; al-Suddī links his action to pity for the aged father; Ibn ʿAṭiyya lists number variants; al-Wāḥidī mentions one bucket poured into a trough."}, {"id": "28:23/q29/p4", "position": "The well was open; Moses pressed through or moved other waterers and used their bucket.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this explains praise of his strength; Ibn Isḥāq says Moses used his strength to get through the crowd."}, {"id": "28:23/q29/p5", "position": "He moved the women's animals forward and watered them.", "reasons": "Study Quran calls this the plain sense; al-Qushayrī says he watered after the shepherds left and withdrew to a wall's shade."}, {"id": "28:23/q29/p6", "position": "The stone story is often dismissed.", "reasons": "Study Quran reports al-Rāzī's objection without specifying its grounds."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q30", "question": "What are the reported circumstances around Moses' arrival and later marriage?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q30/p1", "position": "He fled Egypt after killing the Egyptian, arrived in Midian, helped the women, and married one sister.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾ summarizes the sequence; Study Quran notes years of service to the father-in-law and cites 28:24–28."}, {"id": "28:23/q30/p2", "position": "Midianites' Arab kinship and language with Israelites make their aid to Moses plausible.", "reasons": "Kur'an Yolu offers this historical explanation."}, {"id": "28:23/q30/p3", "position": "Shuʿayb wept from longing for God; God restored his sight and honored him with Moses' ten years of service.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayrī presents this as a narrative report, including promises of Paradise or safety from Hell."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q31", "question": "What does the episode imply about speaking to unrelated women?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q31/p1", "position": "A man may speak with unrelated women for a real need when safe from temptation or harm.", "reasons": "Al-Jishumī states the condition; Abū Ḥayyān and al-Ālūsī infer permission from Moses' question; Bursawī grounds Moses' safety in prophetic protection and compares a Prophet marrying without witnesses."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q32", "question": "What does the daughters' tending livestock teach about women's work and public conduct?", "turns_on": "How broadly to extend the conduct as a legal precedent and how custom and need affect it.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q32/p1", "position": "Their public work is permissible, especially from need, with modest conduct; custom affects propriety.", "reasons": "Al-Kashshāf and Abū Ḥayyān distinguish Bedouin and settled customs; al-Ālūsī says a prophet's allowance is not forbidden; Ibn ʿĀshūr derives a woman's property management and public appearance while covering what must be covered from un-abrogated prior law."}, {"id": "28:23/q32/p2", "position": "Their work was compelled by necessity and illustrates separate spheres for men and women.", "reasons": "Iṣlāḥī says they stayed apart and criticizes reformers advocating identical work spheres."}, {"id": "28:23/q32/p3", "position": "The episode supplies precedents for livelihood, marriage guardianship, labor as dower, joining marriage and hire, and lawful hiring.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr lists these as rulings of prior prophetic law unless abrogated."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q33", "question": "What duties and liabilities does a shepherd have?", "turns_on": "Whether the shepherd acted as a trustworthy agent exercising judgment or exceeded authority.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q33/p1", "position": "A trustworthy shepherd is not liable for lost or stolen animals without evidence of betrayal.", "reasons": "Mālik and al-Muhallab treat shepherds and agents as trustees; al-Qurṭubī allows liability for a known corrupt shepherd; Bursawī cites the hadith that everyone is responsible for those in their care and distinguishes human from animal shepherds."}, {"id": "28:23/q33/p2", "position": "A shepherd who slaughters a dying sheep on reasonable judgment is not liable if he brings the slaughtered animal.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Qāsim's view; a report of a girl using a stone and the Prophet allowing its meat supports permissibility."}, {"id": "28:23/q33/p3", "position": "He is liable for such slaughter until he proves its necessity.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Qāsim reports this competing view."}, {"id": "28:23/q33/p4", "position": "Breeding the owner's females without permission does not make the shepherd liable for loss.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Qāsim reasons that breeding develops the owner's property; al-Qurṭubī prefers latitude for conscientious judgment."}, {"id": "28:23/q33/p5", "position": "He is liable for losses caused by breeding without permission.", "reasons": "Ashhab takes the stricter view."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q34", "question": "What marriage payment and delay rules are drawn from Moses' later service?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q34/p1", "position": "At least a quarter dinar should precede consummation, though the marriage remains valid without it.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Qāsim gives the threshold; later Mālikīs recommend advancing all or some dowry."}, {"id": "28:23/q34/p2", "position": "Beginning the agreed shepherd service counts as paying its dower.", "reasons"

{"id": "28:23/q35", "question": "What moral lessons does the Midian encounter teach?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q35/p1", "position": "It commends helping the weak, generous cooperation, compassion, chastity, gratitude, modesty, and fidelity.", "reasons": "Al-Jishumī commends aiding the weak; al-Biqāʿī urges help despite one's own effort; Ibn ʿĀshūr lists Moses' virtues and Shuʿayb's hospitality, protection and gentleness, and urges emulation."}, {"id": "28:23/q35/p2", "position": "One should flee with faith, rely on God, and trust deliverance and provision from oppression.", "reasons": "Al-Jishumī calls oppression a human act, so escape is a meaningful means to salvation."}, {"id": "28:23/q35/p3", "position": "Hardship can preserve and raise righteous prophets and teach detachment from worldly ease.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī compares the material hardship of two prophets."}, {"id": "28:23/q35/p4", "position": "Prophets may go unrecognized by ordinary herdsmen; believers and knowledge of prophetic law are few.", "reasons": "Bursawī draws this lesson from the livestock."}, {"id": "28:23/q35/p5", "position": "Moses' virtues before his mission invite comparison with Muhammad's known character before revelation.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr says this can guide Meccan polytheists toward recognizing revelation."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q36", "question": "What inward meanings are assigned to the Midian water and its figures?", "turns_on": "The symbolic identity of the water's drinkers and of the women.", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q36/p1", "position": "Arrival at Midian's water is an inward arrival at intimacy, gnosis and divine converse.", "reasons": "Abū Bakr b. Ṭāhir says outward water coincides with meeting the elect and inner steadfastness; al-Wāsiṭī contrasts one who merely arrives seeking release from service with one who leads toward encounter. He links Moses' later shade and need in 28:24 to exclusive turning toward God."}, {"id": "28:23/q36/p2", "position": "The water is unveiling; its drinkers are saints and seekers who nourish their faculties and disciples.", "reasons": "Al-Qāshānī gives this first symbolic identification."}, {"id": "28:23/q36/p3", "position": "The water is unveiling; its drinkers are sacred intellects and disembodied spirits nourishing souls and the cosmos.", "reasons": "Al-Qāshānī presents this alternative."}, {"id": "28:23/q36/p4", "position": "The women are theoretical and practical intellects below the spring; their flock is faculties held from unveiling.", "reasons": "Al-Qāshānī says they subsist on rational knowledge and practical philosophy until Moses as heart arrives; they then receive the higher beings' overflow. Their aged father symbolizes spirit."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q37", "question": "What other phonetic variants are reported around this verse?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q37/p1", "position": "The ṣād may be pronounced as zāy or an intermediate sound, a phonetic assimilation without changed meaning.", "reasons": "Ibn Khālawayh relates it to a quiescent ṣād before dāl; al-Ālūsī and Qirāʾāt ER record the variants."}, {"id": "28:23/q37/p2", "position": "A hamza-softening class is cited by association with the passage, though no exact word occurs here.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jazarī lists five readers and alternatives of between-between, wāw, and yāʾ realization."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q38", "question": "How does this verse relate to its sūra and other passages?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q38/p1", "position": "The repeated Moses narrative uses differences of order, wording and detail to add a distinct nuance each time.", "reasons": "Al-Zarkashī compares the separate tellings with Joseph's gathered story and cites 28:3–43."}, {"id": "28:23/q38/p2", "position": "The Midian story follows Moses' flight and leads to his marriage and service.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾ and Study Quran summarize this narrative arc; the next verse 28:24 follows Moses' shade and prayer."}, {"id": "28:23/q38/p3", "position": "The mention of Midian's water illustrates possible nearness to Hell without entering it in 19:71.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī reports ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr's comparison."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q39", "question": "What is reported about the sūra's place of revelation?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q39/p1", "position": "All of al-Qaṣaṣ is Meccan.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jawzī attributes this to al-Ḥasan, ʿAṭāʾ, and ʿIkrima."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q40", "question": "What special response style is illustrated near Moses' question?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q40/p1", "position": "An answer may broaden, narrow, or redirect the question toward what ought to be asked.", "reasons": "Al-Sakkākī calls redirection a wise style; al-Suyūṭī notes that circumstances can require a broader or narrower reply."}]}
{"id": "28:23/q41", "question": "What other lexical comparison is noted with this narrative?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:23/q41/p1", "position": "Wa-ṭafiqa is glossed as intending or setting out, from Roman usage.", "reasons": "Al-Zarkashī reports the comparison; the note does not identify a word in 28:23."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q01", "question": "Who was the father making the offer?", "turns_on": "Reported kinship and names differ; al-Tabari questions their proof.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q01/p1", "position": "Shuayb, the women's father.", "reasons": "Muqatil and Ibn Atiyya's majority identify him; Biqai names Torah equivalents Reuel and Yithro."}, {"id": "28:27/q01/p2", "position": "Shuayb's nephew, named Tharwan, Athrun or Yathrun.", "reasons": "Al-Hasan, Abu Ubayda and Abu Ubayda ibn Abd Allah ibn Masud give variant forms."}, {"id": "28:27/q01/p3", "position": "A righteous man unrelated to Shuayb, or an uncle called father because he acted as one.", "reasons": "Ibn Atiyya reports both."}, {"id": "28:27/q01/p4", "position": "Yathra, Yathrib or Yathribi, lord of Midian.", "reasons": "Ibn Abbas reports vary in Ibn Kathir and al-Durr."}, {"id": "28:27/q01/p5", "position": "His identity cannot be established from the available reports.", "reasons": "Al-Tabari requires compelling transmission."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q02", "question": "Why did the father offer Moses marriage?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q02/p1", "position": "He valued Moses's strength, trust and character after the daughter's report.", "reasons": "Wahidi mentions her account; Abu Hayyan adds detachment, reliance on God and flight from unbelievers; Ibn Jawzi says he was drawn to Moses."}, {"id": "28:27/q02/p2", "position": "The emphatic words reassure and welcome a stranger.", "reasons": "Biqai says a newcomer rarely expects welcome, especially from a leader; Alusi treats the speech as an emphatic explanatory resumption."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q03", "question": "Was this offer itself the marriage contract?", "turns_on": "The wording expresses intent and leaves the bride unnamed.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q03/p1", "position": "It was a proposal; a later contract needed an identified bride and assent.", "reasons": "Kashshaf contrasts an intention with 'I have married you'; Qurtubi says no uncertain spouse or option is allowed; Razi, Ibn Atiyya and Ibn Ashur infer later specification."}, {"id": "28:27/q03/p2", "position": "The account states an intended pact without establishing its legal form.", "reasons": "Bursevi reports this possibility."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q04", "question": "What does unkiḥaka mean?", "turns_on": "Lexical use and legal literal sense are distinguished.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q04/p1", "position": "I will give one daughter to you in marriage.", "reasons": "Zajjaj, Wahidi and Nasafi gloss it; Biqai compares the joined bond to jaws; Ibn Atiyya rejects an objection to the object construction."}, {"id": "28:27/q04/p2", "position": "Nikah can mean intercourse or contract; the contract is the sounder legal literal sense.", "reasons": "Jishumi reports both usages."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q05", "question": "What are the daughters' reported names?", "turns_on": "The reports give differing names and age order.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q05/p1", "position": "Safura or Safuriyya and a sister called Layya, Leya or Labani.", "reasons": "Shuayb al-Jubbai and later transmitters vary in spelling; Ibn Abi Hatim identifies them as the women who held back their flock."}, {"id": "28:27/q05/p2", "position": "Safura or Safra and a sister called Sharafa, Sharfa or Sharqa.", "reasons": "Ibn Ishaq is quoted in different transcriptions."}, {"id": "28:27/q05/p3", "position": "Elder Safra and younger Safira or Sufayra.", "reasons": "Other authorities in Thalabi and Baghawi."}, {"id": "28:27/q05/p4", "position": "Moses's wife was Balaqis.", "reasons": "Al-Husayn ibn Ali in Mujahid."}, {"id": "28:27/q05/p5", "position": "Moses's wife was Safira, daughter of Yathrun.", "reasons": "Ibn Abbas in al-Durr."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q06", "question": "Which daughter did Moses marry?", "turns_on": "Reports differ on the bride's age and identification.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q06/p1", "position": "The younger, often identified as the inviter and Safura or Safuriyya.", "reasons": "Gabriel, Prophetic reports and Baghawi's majority say younger; Abu Dharr mentions her modest conduct. Qurtubi suggests Moses favored her after their encounter."}, {"id": "28:27/q06/p2", "position": "The elder daughter.", "reasons": "Wahb, al-Qushayri and Ibn Jurayj report elder; Ibn Jurayj calls her Safura and the inviter."}, {"id": "28:27/q06/p3", "position": "The daughter who had invited him, without a settled age.", "reasons": "Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd describes Moses checking the father's preference and hearing of her chastity; Ib

{"id": "28:27/q07", "question": "Does hātayn imply other daughters?", "turns_on": "Whether pointing to these two entails additional daughters.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q07/p1", "position": "It points to the two women Moses met, who were present.", "reasons": "Biqai says Moses could consider them; Tabatabai notes their presence; Abu Hayyan denies further daughters follow from it."}, {"id": "28:27/q07/p2", "position": "It suggests the father had other daughters.", "reasons": "Kashshaf and Nasafi infer this; Alusi reports four younger sisters or seven daughters, but calls the demonstrative inconclusive."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q08", "question": "How is the conditional phrase construed?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q08/p1", "position": "ʿAlā introduces a condition; the infinitive clause can be circumstantial to either party.", "reasons": "Damghani and Ibn Ashur note contractual use; Abu Hayyan, Samin and Alusi attach it to father or Moses."}, {"id": "28:27/q08/p2", "position": "The agreement requires Moses's hired labor for eight years.", "reasons": "Yahya, Muqatil, Zajjaj, Wahidi, Baghawi and others give the practical sense."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q09", "question": "What does taʾjuranī mean here?", "turns_on": "The verb is viewed from either the worker's or recipient's side.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q09/p1", "position": "Moses will work for the father as an employee.", "reasons": "Thalabi, Makki, Kashshaf, Razi, Baydawi, Alusi and Ibn Ashur give this sense."}, {"id": "28:27/q09/p2", "position": "Moses will reward or compensate the father with service.", "reasons": "Ibn Qutayba and Tabari compare God's ajr; Farra makes herding the compensation; Kashshaf cites a Prophetic condolence formula."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q10", "question": "What forms or vocalizations of the hiring verb occur?", "turns_on": "Vocalization and derivational forms differ.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q10/p1", "position": "The jīm can take ḍamma or kasra.", "reasons": "Ibn Jawzi attributes both Arabic forms to al-Farra."}, {"id": "28:27/q10/p2", "position": "Ajar(a) gives maʾjūr or muʾjir; ājara gives muʾājir.", "reasons": "Akhfash and Basran grammarians list the forms; al-Mubarrad favors the short verb and distinguishes ijāra from ijār; al-Raghib views the verbs from one or both parties."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q11", "question": "How are the eight ḥijaj parsed?", "turns_on": "The parse tracks the sense assigned to taʾjuranī.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q11/p1", "position": "As an adverbial duration of eight years.", "reasons": "Tabrisi, Nasafi and others allow or adopt this; Samin says it fits hired-work sense."}, {"id": "28:27/q11/p2", "position": "As an object meaning eight years of work or herding.", "reasons": "Razi adopts it; Kashshaf and Abu Hayyan allow it; Samin insists it belongs to the compensation sense."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q12", "question": "What does ḥijaj mean and why use that word?", "turns_on": "The sources distinguish lexical sense, etymology and implied blessing.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q12/p1", "position": "It is the plural of ḥijja, meaning years.", "reasons": "Tabari, Thalabi, Jishumi, Baghawi, Nasafi, Biqai, Alusi and Ibn Ashur agree; Jishumi glosses ajal as appointed time."}, {"id": "28:27/q12/p2", "position": "The year takes its name from the recurring pilgrimage.", "reasons": "Ibn Ashur notes its place near the Arabic year's end; Tabatabai infers Abrahamic pilgrimage among Shuayb's people; Ja'far al-Sadiq cites ḥijaj rather than sinīn."}, {"id": "28:27/q12/p3", "position": "The term auspiciously suggests blessing, provision or yearly pilgrimage.", "reasons": "Biqai offers these associations."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q13", "question": "What work did Moses perform?", "turns_on": "Whether narrative reports specify work left unstated in the verse.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q13/p1", "position": "He tended the father's flock, possibly with other rural work.", "reasons": "Tabari, Farra, Thalabi, Ibn Ishaq and others specify herding; Biqai adds other tasks. Qurtubi's al-Muhallab invokes custom, but Ibn al-Arabi says no sound transmission proves herding."}, {"id": "28:27/q13/p2", "position": "The Qur'an leaves the work unspecified for its narrative purpose.", "reasons": "Ibn Ashur notes Exodus names Jethro's sheep."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q14", "question": "What was the status of the eight years?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q14/p1", "position": "They were the binding minimum.", "reasons": "Ibn Abbas explicitly says obligatory and reasons a prophet would fulfill it; Razi says the contract used the shorter term."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q15", "question": "Was the service dower or a separate condition?", "turns_on": "Who receives the work and whether the narrative abbreviates a separate dower.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q15/p1", "position": "It was the bride's marriage payment or dower.", "reasons": "Tabari, Thalabi and others take the direct exchange; Tabrisi prefers it from surface wording; Ibn Ashur suggests the daughter consented silently or her father could receive her dower."}, {"id": "28:27/q15/p2", "position": "It was a condition benefiting the father, with separate or legally presumed dower.", "reasons": "Mawardi reports this; Bursevi points to 'hire me' rather than 'her'; Kashshaf, Baydawi and Ibn Ashur list separate wages, separate dower or flock ownership."}, {"id": "28:27/q15/p3", "position": "The pact is reported without settling its legal form.", "reasons": "Bursevi reports this; Ibn Ashur calls the verse too ambiguous to prove a current dower rule alone."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q16", "question": "May marriage and hire be combined, or service count as dower?", "turns_on": "Views turn on what qualifies as dower and on the authority of earlier law.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q16/p1", "position": "Yes, specified service may be linked to marriage or count as dower.", "reasons": "Jishumi, Shafii, Ibn Habib, Ashhab and Asbagh allow it; Tabrisi cites surface wording; Ibn Atiyya and Qurtubi cite Qur'an teaching as dower; Ibn Ashur prefers permission and honoring marriage conditions."}, {"id": "28:27/q16/p2", "position": "A free husband's service is not property and cannot be dower; property or a slave's labor can.", "reasons": "Abu Hanifa says the husband is not property; Bursevi says a valid marriage for free labor still owes the normal dower, citing 4:4 and 4:24."}, {"id": "28:27/q16/p3", "position": "The combination is void or rescinded because hire and marriage differ.", "reasons": "Malik and Ibn al-Qasim are quoted; Ibn Habib allows it if the wife is paid first; Ibn Ashur distinguishes effects before and after consummation."}, {"id": "28:27/q16/p4", "position": "It is disliked initially, but an existing pact may stand.", "reasons": "Abu Zayd and another Malik report say so; Ibn Khuwayz Mindad allows service but prefers money."}, {"id": "28:27/q16/p5", "position": "The earlier law is not binding proof for Muslims.", "reasons": "Razi rejects direct inference, listing guardian benefit, no separate woman's consideration and extra conditions as earlier-law possibilities; Bursevi invokes abrogation by 4:4."}, {"id": "28:27/q16/p6", "position": "Valuable services can be dower in principle, though this ambiguous verse alone cannot establish it.", "reasons": "Ibn Ashur calls for legal-principle analysis."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q17", "question": "Must hired work, term and flock be specified?", "turns_on": "Whether custom removes uncertainty.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q17/p1", "position": "Custom can specify ordinary work; the start runs from contract if unstated.", "reasons": "Malik, Bukhari and al-Muhallab cite the general verse; Ibn Atiyya and Qurtubi say negotiations may have set the start. Known months, wages and counted flock are agreed valid."}, {"id": "28:27/q17/p2", "position": "Unnamed tasks or flock are indeterminate and invalid.", "reasons": "Abu Hanifa and Shafii require tasks; Ibn al-Qasim requires replacement terms for an identified flock, which Qurtubi calls very weak."}, {"id": "28:27/q17/p3", "position": "Custom and known shepherd capacity can determine an unspecified flock.", "reasons": "Qurtubi approves knowing capacity, recalling Moses lifting the stone."}]}
{"id": "28:27/q18", "question": "What wage or flock did Moses receive?", "turns_on": "Reports differ in the criterion and miracle details; the text leaves wages unstated.", "positions": [{"id": "28:27/q18/p1", "position": "Lambs unlike their mothers in color; a staff miracle produced them.", "reasons": "Yahya, Mawardi, Tabrisi, Qurtubi and Anas vary over placing or striking the staff, dream instruction, ropes over water and one exception; Thalabi says Shuayb recognized divine provision."}, {"id": "28:27/q18/p2", "position": "Every spotted or piebald lamb; all were spotted.", "reasons": "Yahya, Mawardi, Qurtubi and Thalabi report this variant."}, {"id": "28:27/q18/p3", "position": "The verse leaves the wages unstated; marriage or customary wages are possible.", "reasons": "Ibn Ashur recalls shirts, balagha shoes and other customary shepherd wages; Qurtubi says the wage is unspecified."}, {"id": "28:27/q18/p4", "position": "At departure a miraculous colored flock multiplied for Moses.", "reasons": "Utba's report mentions twins, triplets and later Samaritan sheep in Syria; al-Durr reports colored offspring."}]}
